A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

sialyltransferase from rat liver Golli vesicles can utilize a variety of cholesterol-containing lactose-derived neoglycoliipids, which contain a variety of different linkages and substituents, as acceptors for the synthesis of mono- and disalylated products.

The main takeaway from our work is that
neoglycolipsids containing a lactose moiety and a cholesterol moiety can be used as acceptors in the sialylation of the lactosyl residue.
cholesterol-containing neoglycoliptids can be used as acceptors to synthesize sialylated neoglycoliplids.
cholesterol-containing lactose derivatives can serve as acceptors of sialic acid and are thus potential acceptors for the synthesis of gangliosides and related molecules.
